name: scratchpad-note-taking
context: Long-running multi-step tasks where the agent accumulates intermediate findings, partial results, and reminders that must survive across tool calls and context resets. The agent writes notes to persistent external storage and reads them back at relevant moments, preventing the context window from being cluttered with verbose intermediate traces. Unlike episodic memory (past episodes), scratchpad is active working memory for the current task.
benefits: Keeps context window lean by offloading intermediate reasoning
Survives context resets and compaction events
Makes the agent's internal state inspectable from outside
Enables progressive disclosure — agent reveals notes to user on demand
tradeoffs: Extra tool calls to write and read notes
Note format and retrieval strategy must be designed carefully
Stale notes can mislead if not invalidated on context changes
Adds implementation complexity over bare context accumulation
use_cases: Complex coding tasks where the agent must track file changes across many edits
Research agents that build a persistent notes file over a multi-session investigation
Customer support agents that maintain case notes across turns
Autonomous agents running long dungeon explorations or training sequences
avoid_when: Tasks that fit entirely within the context window
Environments where external file writes are not available
anti_patterns: Writing raw tool outputs verbatim instead of distilled findings
Never reading notes back — writing-only scratchpad
Notes that grow without bound (same compaction problem)
design_principles: Write findings, not transcripts — distill, do not append
Index notes by task phase or file so retrieval is targeted
Treat notes as ephemeral — they do not survive session boundaries without explicit persistence
best_practices: Use a structured format (JSON or Markdown) for machine-readable notes
Validate notes on read — check staleness before trusting
Expose notes to the user via a read tool so they can follow the agent's reasoning
references: Nye et al., Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation in Language Models, 2021 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.00114
Anthropic, Effective Context Engineering for AI Agents, 2025 — https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
